title: Built by Lawyers, Tailored by You: Harvey Launches Purpose-Built Legal Agents Across Every Major Practice Area
author: Harvey Team

dom.t: Vertical AI: Commercial traction cannot prove defensibility

st.t: Professional tasks: Partial credit overstates complete success
st.an: The source aligns with task-specific evaluation by describing agents built for defined legal tasks and pressure-tested against practical work. However, it also markets one-click, client-ready deliverables without reproducible methods, independent measurements, or evidence of complete-task success, which conflicts with the cluster’s caution against inferring production competence from internal testing and broad quality claims.

st.t: Harvey strategy: Prestige supports infrastructure ambitions
st.an: The source reinforces Harvey’s infrastructure strategy by presenting customizable agents as a mechanism for encoding and scaling distinctive legal practices across substantive workflows. Its reported agent creation and platform reach add concrete evidence of rollout and commercial adoption, while remaining company-reported indicators that do not establish accuracy, productivity, intensive use or security performance.
qs: "Now every legal team can do the same: take what makes their practice distinctive and turn it into agents that scale."  Legal teams have created more than 25,000 custom agents on Harvey.
Our products streamline workflows in areas including contract analysis, due diligence, compliance, and litigation to drive efficiency and value.

st.t: Power users: Usage volume may obscure value
st.an: The source accepts that value depends on workflow integration, governance and outcome-focused implementation rather than access or usage volume alone. It materially extends the proposition with a concrete model for encoding organisation-specific expertise into reusable agents while reserving legal judgment for lawyers, though its effectiveness claims remain largely unquantified.

kp.k: Agent library expands automation into longer legal workflows
kp.d: Harvey announces 500+ ready-to-use legal agents and an upgraded Agent Builder on May 5, 2026. The company claims the upgrades handle longer processes and generate Word, Powerpoint, and Excel deliverables, extending automation from discrete assistance toward intake-to-deliverable workflows. Availability is qualified: the blog specifies early access for select customers, while the release describes wider availability over the upcoming months.
qs: Today, we're introducing a major upgrade to Harvey's agentic platform: a library of 500+ ready-to-use agents built and tested by lawyers, and an improved Agent Builder for teams that want to customize agents to reflect their organization’s unique expertise.
These upgrades can handle longer processes and produce Word, Powerpoint, and Excel files, helping lawyers move from intake to client-ready deliverables in a single click.
500 agents and Agent Builder are in early access today, May 5, and will be available to Harvey customers on an ongoing basis over the upcoming months.

kp.k: Agents target procurement, funds, investigations and other practices
kp.d: Harvey describes task-specific agents across M&A, funds, in-house procurement, employment, IP and white collar investigations. Illustrative capabilities include extracting vendor obligations and deadlines, comparing dozens of side letters against an LP agreement and drafting a memorandum, and cross-checking employee testimony against documents to flag inconsistencies, build credibility tables and recommend follow-up. These are vendor descriptions of capabilities rather than reported outcome studies.
qs: Every agent in Harvey's library is purpose-built for a specific legal task, covering global practice groups from M&A and funds to in-house procurement, labor and employment, IP, white collar investigations, and more.
In-house teams can quickly review vendor agreements, summarize key terms, and surface any upcoming deadlines or actions, so that they can take the appropriate next steps.
Funds teams can review dozens of side letters in one step, making it much easier to identify any deviations in terms and draft a summary in a new memorandum.
Lawyers can progress an internal investigation by cross-checking employee testimonies, asking the agent to flag inconsistencies, create a credibility table, and recommend follow-up steps.

kp.k: Customization embeds organizational expertise into repeatable agents
kp.d: Harvey says teams can modify library agents in plain English, changing scope and steps and incorporating their own context, precedents and expertise, or describe an agent to build from scratch. Chief Product Officer Anique Drumright frames this as enabling teams to scale what distinguishes their practice, with options ranging from immediate use of prebuilt workflows to organization-specific deployment.
qs: With the latest Agent Builder update, you can take any agent from the library and tailor it in plain english by adjusting scope, refining steps, and adding your organization's specific context, precedents, and expertise.
If you want to build something from scratch, you can describe what you need and ask Harvey to build it for you.
Now every legal team can do the same: take what makes their practice distinctive and turn it into agents that scale.

kp.k: Lawyer-led development and testing underpin claimed workflow quality
kp.d: Harvey attributes agent development and pressure-testing to its internal lawyers and says design-partner firms helped shape capabilities and quality requirements. The release claims testing against evaluation benchmarks for accuracy and relevance, but supplies no benchmark names, methods, scores or study details.
qs: Each one was developed and pressure-tested by our internal team of lawyers against the same tasks and nuances legal professionals face in practice.
These capabilities were built alongside design partners: leading firms who worked directly with us to shape what this next generation of agents needed to do and the quality bar they had to clear.

The combination of ready-to-use agents, built for and by lawyers and tested against evaluation benchmarks for accuracy and relevance, and robust customization options within Agent Builder means that Harvey can support any legal organization's agentic needs.

kp.k: Process delegation is paired with retained lawyer judgment
kp.d: Harvey frames agents as handling routine processes so lawyers can concentrate on strategic guidance, while explicitly retaining lawyer judgment. CEO Winston Weinberg separately characterizes the industry as already moving beyond AI assistants into legal agents. This is the vendor's account of professional role change, not evidence of measured workforce restructuring or autonomous replacement of lawyers.
qs: When routine work is handled, lawyers can focus on the strategic guidance that actually drives better outcomes.
The agents handle the process. You own the judgment.
The legal industry is now well past AI as an assistant and officially in the era of legal agents,

kp.k: Customer emphasizes governance and shared client workflows
kp.d: In a customer quotation carried by Harvey, Willkie Farr & Gallagher's Chief Digital and Information Officer John Elbasan says the firm is applying agentic capabilities across complex litigation, corporate and financial services matters and adjacent practices. He describes a feedback loop with Harvey, emphasizes governance and reliability, and argues that shared platforms can facilitate collaboration with adopting clients. His account makes value conditional on integration, governance and outcome-focused application.
qs: The partnership creates a continuous feedback loop that helps shape how these capabilities evolve in practice, with a strong emphasis on governance, reliability, and real-world application, benefiting both our clients and the broader legal community,

As more clients adopt platforms like Harvey, we are able to meet them in those same environments and work more seamlessly together, reinforcing that the value of these technologies depends on how they are integrated into workflows, governed appropriately, and applied with a clear focus on outcomes.

kp.k: Harvey reports substantial custom-agent creation and platform reach
kp.d: The May 5, 2026 release reports that legal teams have created more than 25,000 custom agents and that Harvey's platform is trusted by more than 100,000 lawyers across 1,500 organizations. It says new agents are added regularly as lawyers and customers identify use cases. These company-reported figures describe agent creation and platform reach, without quantifying active agent usage, productivity gains or changes in legal employment.
qs: Legal teams have created more than 25,000 custom agents on Harvey.
New agents are added regularly as lawyers and customers identify emerging use cases.
All agents run on Harvey's secure platform, which is trusted by more than 100,000 lawyers across 1,500 organizations.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Harvey claims its upgraded agents automate longer legal workflows through production of client-ready documents.
pts.d: The Harvey Team describes a library of more than 500 task-specific agents covering practice areas including M&A, funds, procurement, employment, IP and investigations. Claimed capabilities include extracting vendor-contract obligations and deadlines, comparing dozens of side letters with an LP agreement and drafting a memorandum, and cross-checking employee statements against documents to flag inconsistencies, construct a credibility table and recommend follow-up steps. These are presented as current product capabilities, not as measured productivity outcomes.

pts.k: Harvey claims plain-language agent customization lets legal teams scale their distinctive expertise and processes.
pts.d: The Harvey Team says users can modify existing agents' scope and steps, incorporate organizational context and precedents, or describe a new task and have Harvey build an agent. Chief Product Officer Anique Drumright frames this as enabling legal teams to translate their distinctive practice knowledge into scalable agents. The press release presents ready-made and customized agents as options spanning immediate deployment through tailored organizational rollout.

pts.k: Harvey describes a shift from AI assistance to delegated processes while retaining lawyers' judgment.
pts.d: CEO Winston Weinberg characterizes the legal industry as already in an era of agents rather than assistants. The Harvey Team claims that delegating routine work frees lawyers to concentrate on strategic guidance and better outcomes. Despite its single-click deliverable language, the source expressly reserves judgment for lawyers; it does not claim complete replacement of lawyers or specify human verification procedures.

pts.k: Willkie's John Elbasan says agent adoption enables substantive legal applications and more seamless client collaboration, with value dependent on implementation and governance.
pts.d: Elbasan, Willkie Farr & Gallagher's Chief Digital and Information Officer, reports use of agentic capabilities in complex litigation, corporate and financial services work. He says the innovation partnership provides a feedback loop for development and that shared platforms allow the firm to collaborate more seamlessly with adopting clients. These statements are attributed to Elbasan as a participating firm's account, rather than to PR Newswire.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers internal lawyer testing, unspecified evaluation benchmarks, design-partner involvement and a participating firm's experience.
pts.d: Harvey says its internal lawyers developed and pressure-tested the agents against practical legal tasks and that agents were tested for accuracy and relevance. It names Gowling WLG, Willkie, Clayton Utz, Mallesons and Hengeler Mueller as design partners. Drumright invokes designers' experience doing the underlying work; Elbasan supplies a qualitative account of deployment. The document provides no benchmark names, methods, scores, measured time savings or quantified client outcomes.

pts.k: Harvey supplies self-reported adoption and platform-scale figures as context for its agent rollout.
pts.d: The press release reports more than 25,000 custom agents created by legal teams, more than 100,000 lawyers across 1,500 organizations using or trusting the platform, and a customer footprint across more than 60 countries. These figures describe creation and platform reach; they do not establish how frequently agents are used or quantify workflow quality or efficiency gains.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The capabilities are announced as current on May 5, 2026, but access is initially restricted and broader availability is phased.
pts.d: The blog describes what agents can do 'today' while specifying early access for select customers. The press release states that the agents and Agent Builder are in early access on May 5, with availability extending to Harvey customers over the following months. Additional agents are to be added regularly as use cases emerge. Weinberg's industry-transition statement is a present-tense characterization, not a dated future forecast.

pts.k: The claimed benefits depend on organizational tailoring, appropriate governance and workflow integration.
pts.d: Harvey links preservation of distinctive expertise to adding organizational context, precedents and processes. Elbasan explicitly conditions technological value on workflow integration, governance and outcome-focused application, and links improved shared-platform collaboration to further client adoption. The source's division of responsibility leaves judgment with lawyers even as agents execute processes.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The stated beneficiaries are law firms, in-house legal teams and their clients across multiple practice areas.
pts.d: Harvey, a legal-technology provider, targets both provider-side law firms and buyer-side corporate legal departments. In-house teams are promised quicker vendor-agreement review and obligation tracking; funds lawyers are promised batch side-letter comparison and memorandum drafting; investigation lawyers are promised evidence comparison and suggested follow-up. Organizations can embed their expertise in reusable agents, while lawyers retain strategic judgment. Elbasan also identifies benefits to clients and the broader legal community. The document does not make specific claims about staffing reductions, legal fees or access to justice.
